title: Write from vetted material, not from scratch
statement: Have a model assemble, adapt and cite vetted sources, carrying over what they specify rather than inventing items from scratch.
example: In a study of 9 AI quiz builders cited in one project's generator notes, 74% of the items had major flaws and only 1 in 5 was usable.
detail: A reading project's generator notes set out an asymmetry: models are reliable at tagging and assembling (tagging hits ~87–95%) and unreliable at authoring, since of 9 Gen-AI quiz builders studied, 80% of items violated at least one best-practice guideline and 74% had major flaws (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/generator-insights.md`, B1). They conclude that generators should assemble and transform vetted material and tag it to standards, not invent items from scratch, and that every generation should be grounded in a source the generator cites, since ungrounded generation is where the 74%-flaw rate lives (B3). It bears on a learning from the AP work, that a writer should get verified facts as its only source, not as inspiration. The same notes say to treat what a generator makes as a candidate until a separate check passes it.
against: the study of 9 quiz builders is cited second-hand, with no DOI or URL in these files; and generated items can still serve once gated: construction-first generation survived the anti-leak gate at 60% vs 6% for encyclopedic clones, and one production campaign certified 48.7% (738 of 1,516), while raw generated banks leaked ~94% blind (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/practice-layer-spec.md`). In a fifth-grade course's history, construction-first generation survived the anti-leak gate at 60% vs 6% for encyclopedic clones (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/practice-layer-spec.md`).

**Treat generator output as *candidate* until a separate check passes.**

A 2025 effectiveness study of nine Gen-AI quiz builders found that 80 percent of the 270 multiple-choice items they produced violated at least one best-practice guideline, and 74 percent had “major” flaws likely to invalidate results.
